column8: Tue 17 Nov: References or store only; Rippl's first line names any store's job, but the reserve serves ten dated draws and only runs down (row 41), so never an image beside the conceit.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a evidence clause or References; Rippl (1883): the worst run, not the driest year, sets the store, which shows why the test holds cash waiting at zero for all sixteen years; say it shows why, never that the test came from Rippl; one plain clause, no water image (tonight's voice round).

Tue 17 Nov: store; size once because no later deposit comes and IPS l.11 keeps shares from the ten; $35,894: check after tonight's re-size (working NUMBERS 2 already reads $36,774); in prose say the extra Treasuries.

Tue 17 Nov: store; Rippl's running total is NUMBERS 2's year-by-year ledger, solved there by an exact linear programme (USACE lists LP); textbook hydrology, so R 3; in prose the extra Treasuries, never backstop (WORDS).

Tue 17 Nov: 3e or Table 3 store; the quoted phrase is in this morning's NUMBERS 2 but gone from tonight's working copy, where the 0.5% margin is spent on the same 2036 and 2037 payments (8a: the carry runs out after 2035); check after tonight's re-size and quote the new wording.

Tue 17 Nov: store only; evaporation as the fee's twin is a second image (tonight's voice round: every second image failed), and costs beyond the fee not yet in the payments' sum goes stale with tonight's 0.5% margin: check after tonight's re-size.

Tue 17 Nov: Figure 1's note or 3a store; USACE's firm yield touches empty exactly once, as the extra Treasuries end with nothing spare under the standard, so touching zero in the stress is the design, not a flaw; exactly $0 spare: check after tonight's re-size (the standard now carries the 0.5% fund-cost margin); a source, no water words in prose.

Tue 17 Nov: store; firm against safe helps Keel think, but water's not guaranteed beside Treasuries muddles Book 19's words and the Wed 18 Nov re-size clause is stale: check after tonight's re-size, then say what the standard covers, never firm or safe yield in prose.

Tue 17 Nov: store; Texas buys a water margin by promising about a sixth less from the same lake (85% and 82%, Keel arithmetic checked), Laura buys hers with more Treasuries because $50,000 cannot shrink; a contrast for questions, not prose.

Tue 17 Nov: guard for WORDS; a science board's warning that firm yield is misleadingly called safe supports naming the standard (even if cash waiting earns nothing) over calling the reserve safe; Treasuries may still be called guaranteed (Book 19).

Tue 17 Nov: store; a drought of record persuades because it happened; the plan's standard has history too (two eras of waiting cash near zero, NUMBERS 8a) but is harsher, so never call it a drought-of-record standard.
Tue 17 Nov: References or store; Klemes (1979): the method is neutral and the input sets the standard, the line that keeps the parallel honest (the plan feeds in zero less the fee, not a record).

Tue 17 Nov: store, the sourced form of H8-042: LCRA sells firm and interruptible water at two prices; but LCRA contracts its interruptible water and her flexibility is promised to no one, so never call her flexibility interruptible.
Tue 17 Nov: store; 2012's first cut-off shows interruptible water is a buffer for firm customers; her flexibility is never a buffer for the ten (IPS l.11, Q59's kill), so a contrast only.

Tue 17 Nov: store; certainty has a price in water too, but the use says most of Laura's price returns to her, which 3a's one wording forbids (never most comes back); $35,894 and $45,456: check after tonight's re-size (working NUMBERS 2: $36,774 and $46,566).
Tue 17 Nov: LCRA's commit-only-firm definition is row 17's idea in a weaker form (a utility's plan, not a statute); its April 2015 near-empty storage travels with row 21.

Tue 17 Nov: 3c/3d store or one clause; Kansas law forbids contracting past the drought yield and leaves the rest uncommitted, a second public precedent beside the Antideficiency rule (Q43-009), never both; statute read only as quoted in KGS Bulletin 239, so S 4; never in all but name.

Tue 17 Nov: store; Texas counts only firm supply against needs and lets no two projects rely on the same water, the outside twin of Q5c-024 (the extra Treasuries serve the ten, never the range, NUMBERS 8h); never backstop in prose.

Tue 17 Nov: store; England's deployable output leaves out drought measures and counts only contracts, as the range counts only owned Treasuries; one of four count-only-firm rows, row 17 the strongest.

Tue 17 Nov: store; LCRA writes down what happens past its design drought, but the IPS's two reasons are the only two flows the plan does not own, not its answer to a beaten standard (fund costs past 0.5% or waiting rates below the test leave a small shortfall and no plan change); never the two reasons as a curtailment rule.

Tue 17 Nov: 3c or 3e store; a beaten record cut LCRA's firm yield by about a sixth for future sales while existing contracts stood, the outside form of aha row 4 (a fall shrinks the next figure, never one stated); say it plainly with no ink (tonight's voice round: no second image); read in a repost, so S 4.

Tue 17 Nov: store; water managers cannot tell in time whether they are past the design drought; but Table 3 has no row checking the bill rate each month, so drop the Table 3 claim unless the exhibits owner adds one; the standard is a stated condition, not a watched trigger.
Tue 17 Nov: Texas 2011, the worst single year yet not the drought of record, is Rippl's lesson again; keep as row 2's second example.

Tue 17 Nov: store; the climatologist's line is good, but its use sets the 919-start replay as a test passed, which Q81-013 and aha row 5 forbid (it follows from the fee test): say only the margin, at least $2,454 left (NUMBERS 8a).
Tue 17 Nov: store only; a correction to the card's claim 3 (Spicewood Beach ran dry on wells, not a firm-yield reservoir); news pages, so S 3.

Tue 17 Nov: store; Cape Town's 1-in-50 standard was beaten by a roughly 1-in-311 drought, so no drought-of-record failure; Laura's standard is a stated condition, never a 1-in-N (no probability rarer than 1 in 100 in prose).

Tue 17 Nov: 3a candidate for the next cold aha test; Cape Town would not plan on no rain, Laura's reserve plans on no interest for the money it does not own, affordable because the rest is written into Treasuries; fix: one plain evidence clause, no rain image, never any engineer is allowed (one city's judgement), the inflow it does not own rather than one uncertain inflow (fund costs too); $35,894: check after tonight's re-size.

Tue 17 Nov: store; Cape Town survived by drawing less, which Laura's fixed $50,000 cannot do (IPS l.11); a contrast for questions; which is why her standard sits below history is Keel's reading, not a recorded reason.

Tue 17 Nov: store; Melbourne's 2006 flows fell about 30% below the previous lowest, a record beaten by a wide margin; with row 36 it backs 3e's can be beaten, carrying the guard that rates abroad went further below zero (Q2d).
Tue 17 Nov: the source of row 41's first break (a reservoir refills, the reserve only runs down, NUMBERS 8h); travels with row 41.

Tue 17 Nov: store; Melbourne's one weather-proof source covers only part of demand while the Treasuries cover all ten with no interest on waiting money; five payments come through funds, whose payouts are never called fixed.

Tue 17 Nov: store; abstract only, S 3; fix the use: the test sits just below the worst twelve months on record (-0.15% against -0.126%, Q81-012), so never a test the record never came near, and no ink beside a water source.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e store or one plain evidence clause; USBR: firm yield is neither absolute nor fixed, an assumed volume; drop water's firm is pencil (a conceit turn on a second parallel, tonight's voice round) and say only that a figure her Treasuries pay cannot be rewritten by a new record.

Tue 17 Nov: store; 2% a year is about 28% over sixteen years (Keel arithmetic checked), so a 1-in-N standard sounds stricter than it is; supports stating the condition, never a 1-in-N; never mixed with the 585 starting months.

Tue 17 Nov: the design drought moves a reservoir's yield by tens of percent, row 33's point; its plan comparison (covered at 0.06% a year) is the pre-margin record: check after tonight's re-size, and never a few hundred dollars (SKELETON 3c).
Tue 17 Nov: store or a 3e source; English water moved from the worst drought seen to a 1-in-500 standard by 2039/40; supports set below history, never that the plan's standard cannot be beaten.

Tue 17 Nov: store; the plan uses a bound where money is promised and modelled odds only before the move (NUMBERS 8p); a judge may read firm yield's replacement as the bound being outdated, so never cite it without the disanalogy that her inflows are written into Treasuries; Hazen not read.

Tue 17 Nov: 3c/3d store; California's Table A, a stated maximum delivered at 5% three times in nine years, is what a figure stated above what is owned becomes; aha row 4 is the one home of that principle, so one clause at most, never beside Kansas (row 17).

Tue 17 Nov: 3a or Figure 1's note; the extra Treasuries are a firm-yield sizing on a harsher input, but any water plan may use overclaims (row 27), the firm-not-safe clause and exactly zero once need a check after tonight's re-size, and evaporation is a second image; never backstop in prose.

Tue 17 Nov: restates Q81-011, Q81-012, Q81-031 and Q2d-016; its guards travel with Q81-031: say over any twelve months (bills closed below zero on 8 days), never cannot be beaten, never paid in all 919 starts as evidence; its fund-cost clause is stale: check after tonight's re-size.
Tue 17 Nov: guard for any use of the parallel in 3b or 3e: say the reserve only runs down and its leftover returns to Laura; $45,456 and $0 under the test: check after tonight's re-size.

Tue 17 Nov: guard, confirmed by tonight's voice round (every second image set up in a sentence failed): the reservoir parallel is evidence, a reference or one plain clause, never a second image and never in a passage with a pencil-and-ink turn; like defence in depth, a source with no water words.
